blocks.prompt: 6 Show that \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\) has a relative minimum at \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh "show that" wala sawal hai; diye gaye point par relative minimum saabit karna hai.
Diya: \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\), sirf \(x > 0\) par defined. Yahan \(x\) base mein bhi hai aur power mein bhi.
Rule: aise function ka derivative logarithmic differentiation se nikalta hai (2.6); phir Second Derivative Test.
Plan: \(\ln\) le kar \(f'\), dikhana ke point par \(f' = 0\), phir \(f'' > 0\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\), \(x > 0\).
Saabit karna: \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\) par relative minimum.
Tareeqa: \(x^{x^{2}}\) par na power rule lagta hai (power constant nahin) na exponential rule (base constant nahin). Is liye pehle logarithm lete hain, phir Second Derivative Test.

Logarithm lein
Maan lijiye \(y = x^{x^{2}}\).
\[\ln y = x^{2}\ln x\]
Kyun: \(\ln a^{b} = b\ln a\): power neeche aa kar multiply ho jati hai, aur mushkil shakal ek product ban jati hai.

Derivative
\[\dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\ln x + x^{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[f'(x) = x^{x^{2}}\,x\,(1 + 2\ln x)\]
\[= x^{x^{2} + 1}(1 + 2\ln x)\]
Kyun: left side par implicit differentiation (\(\ln y\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}\)), right side par product rule. Phir dono taraf \(y = x^{x^{2}}\) se multiply kiya. \(2x\ln x + x = x(1 + 2\ln x)\).

Stationary point
\[1 + 2\ln x = 0 \Rightarrow \ln x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[x = e^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\]
Kyun: \(x > 0\) par \(x^{x^{2} + 1}\) hamesha positive, is liye sirf bracket zero ho sakta hai. Pehli shart poori.

Point par doosra derivative
\(f'(x) = g(x)h(x)\) likhein, jahan \(g = x^{x^{2} + 1}\) aur \(h = 1 + 2\ln x\):
\[f''(x) = g'(x)h(x) + g(x)h'(x)\]
\(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\) par \(h = 0\) aur \(h' = \frac{2}{x}\):
\[f''\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = x^{x^{2} + 1} \cdot \dfrac{2}{x} = 2x^{x^{2}}\]
Kyun: product rule. Pehli term \(g'h\) mein \(h = 0\) hai, is liye woh khud gayab; \(g'\) ka lamba formula nikaalne ki zaroorat hi nahin. Yeh ek kaam ki chalaaki hai.

Is ka sign
\[x^{2} = \dfrac{1}{e},\quad x^{x^{2}} = \left(e^{-1/2}\right)^{1/e} = e^{-\frac{1}{2e}}\]
\[f''\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 2e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} > 0\]
Kyun: \(e\) ki har power positive hoti hai. \(f'' > 0\), yani seedha pyala: relative minimum. Doosri shart bhi poori.
Dhyan dein: \(\left(e^{-1/2}\right)^{1/e} = e^{-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{e}}\); powers multiply hoti hain.

Minimum value
\[f\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} \approx 0.832\]
Kyun: yeh wahi \(x^{x^{2}}\) hai jo upar nikala.

Tasdeeq: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}} \approx 0.607\). Qareeb ke points: \(f(0.5) = 0.5^{0.25} \approx 0.841\) aur \(f(0.7) = 0.7^{0.49} \approx 0.839\); dono 0.832 se bare hain, jaisa minimum ke paas hona chahiye.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(f'\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 0\) aur \(f''\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\right) = 2e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} > 0\), is liye \(f(x) = x^{x^{2}}\) ka \(x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{e}}\) par relative minimum hai (minimum value \(e^{-\frac{1}{2e}} \approx 0.832\)).
